person.subtitle: Focusing on mechanistic interpretability, neurosymbolic AI, and responsible AI
person.description: Reverse-engineering neural networks with neurosymbolic methods: sparse autoencoders, logic-guided circuit discovery, and provable explanations of graph neural networks. Assessing explainability for AI regulation.
about: I am a PhD student at the Intelligent Data Analysis Lab, Faculty of Electrical Engineering at the Czech Technical University in Prague, supervised by Gustav Šír. My research is on neurosymbolic mechanistic interpretability: logic-guided circuit discovery, sparse feature learning, and provably sufficient explanations of graph neural networks. Previously, I worked on symmetry-invariant deep learning and binarized GNNs for combinatorial optimization.

This autumn (Sep–Dec 2026), I am an Applied Research Intern at Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), using natural language autoencoders to explain AI-text detectors and AI humanizer models. Since July 2026, I have also taken part in the EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR), studying sparse autoencoder pathologies that mimic feature hierarchy.

I am passionate about developing AI in a more responsible way. I co-founded Responsible AI in Prague, an initiative organizing talks, debates, and the First Prague Workshop on Responsible AI. Our research assesses explainability methods for AI governance; we derived XAI desiderata from the EU AI Act.

Beyond research, I have 5+ years of industry ML engineering experience, from NLP models to shipped LLM applications (RAG, tools, guardrails), most recently at Leeaf, where I built an IVF patient assistant and a psychological-support app.

In 2024, I received a master's degree in artificial intelligence with honors from the Czech Technical University, including an Erasmus+ exchange at Aalto University. In 2021, I graduated from the prg.ai Minor program, completing interdisciplinary AI courses across Prague universities. I review for NeurIPS, ICANN, and the Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence journal, serve on the CTU Ethics Committee, and am the president of the Czech Alpha Chapter of Upsilon Pi Epsilon (UPE). In spring 2026, I was a teaching assistant for the new Machine Learning Methods course.
